I think a large part of the problem was that there was no government-to-government discussion prior to releasing the Cole memo. And the vague "some tribes" requesting guidance struck people as hinky.

That is a keen insight, but I'd still recommend that each tribe simply releases policy for their own lands. That projects a strong leadership presence that communicates, "We're in control of our people and in charge of our destinies."

Note that this is all a totally separate thing from prohibition itself, which I oppose. But they could do good on that front by demonstrating a saner approach to it than juggernaut prison industry. Imagine if the result of this is that we read future articles about how tribes are showing up the feds with smarter policy.

Getting upset about the memo does exactly the opposite. It casts their leaders as reactionary, controlled by trends among federal officials; trends that could be temporary. No matter what the banter or gossip is in D.C., any sovereign government that isn't in D.C. should project independence.

That said, the tribes will ultimately decide their own policies, here. They may indeed go with a less draconian approach, sure. But they may not.
